description: Add signed Slack Retry recovery and single-winner multi-Bot selection with durable authorization, dispatch, and Block Kit presentation.

tasks.title: Generalize the signed Slack interaction and adapter pass-through boundary
tasks.spec: specs/slack-failure-retry-action/spec.md#The adapter forwards Retry controls without interpreting them
tasks.description: Extract the existing v1 Slack action signing and verification rules into a shared Server-owned boundary that can issue and validate Retry and Bot-selection payloads while preserving signed Stop behavior. Extend the interaction result and delivery-reference contract so action handlers can return stable operation outcomes and Server-owned Block Kit updates, make replayed interactions re-enter a pending operation instead of stopping at a duplicate receipt, and keep the mohist-slack adapter as an acknowledgement-plus-pass-through transport.
acceptanceCriteria: The shared action codec canonicalizes every authorization-relevant field, omits Slack credentials from serialized values, signs with the verified Connection credential, and verifies signatures with constant-time comparison for Stop, Retry, and selection payload shapes.

SlackInteractionRoutes accepts only normalized block_actions envelopes, delegates authorization and routing to the Server, and uses the stable operation or prompt reference returned by the action handler for idempotent presentation updates; unsupported actions still produce an explicit rejection without runtime work.

mohist-slack acknowledges a block_actions event before forwarding it, preserves the action ID, signed value, actor, and Slack context byte-for-byte at the contract boundary, omits raw Slack payloads and credentials, and delivers Server-provided text and blocks unchanged through chat.update; it does not interpret candidates or authorize actions. A replayed interaction still reaches the Server operation/presentation path and is not suppressed solely because a receipt already exists.

Server and adapter contract tests cover canonicalization and tamper detection, credential omission, prompt acknowledgement ordering, exact action-field forwarding, exact result-block delivery, and regression of the existing signed Stop interaction.
The focused Server Slack interaction tests and the mohist-slack typecheck and test suite pass without real Slack credentials or network access.
tasks.output: Shared Server-signed Slack action contract, stable interaction result plumbing, adapter pass-through behavior, and passing regression tests.
tasks.notes: Keep authorization and routing in Server code. The selection capability has a corresponding adapter requirement in specs/slack-multi-bot-selection/spec.md; its concrete action and prompt behavior is delivered by T-003.

tasks.title: Deliver signed Retry recovery for failed Slack executions
tasks.spec: specs/slack-failure-retry-action/spec.md#Failed Slack results expose a signed Retry action
tasks.description: Enrich Connection-owned terminal failure facts with authoritative session, input, turn, and retryability data, then add the durable Slack retry-operation record and migration. Implement the exact retryability category policy, Retry creation, Server-side authorization and terminal-state revalidation, pre-dispatch operation claiming, an explicit retry-key launcher contract for root attempts, threaded follow-up dispatch through the existing Session, a fixed-key recovery reminder for committed pending operations, and idempotent Slack status replacement with the appropriate Stop control.
acceptanceCriteria: A retryable failed Slack terminal presentation contains readable sanitized failure evidence and exactly one Server-generated signed Retry action bound to the Connection, session or work target, failed input or turn, dispatch reference, workspace, conversation, message, optional thread, actor, nonce, and expiry; the exact allowlist is runner-unavailable, runner-lost, report-timeout, timeout, deadline-exceeded, probe_timeout, opencode-transport-failed, unavailable-runtime, rate_limited, and retry-safe; completed, cancelled, unknown, category-less, unrecognized, non-retryable, and legacy terminal events do not expose Retry.

Tampered, malformed, expired, wrong-Connection, wrong-workspace, wrong-conversation, wrong-message or thread, and unauthorized Retry submissions return explicit invalid, expired, stale, or unauthorized outcomes, enqueue only the explanatory presentation update, and invoke no runtime control, launch, or fresh-attempt dispatch.

A valid Retry re-reads the authoritative session provenance and failed-turn state before effect, creates a new root Session plus initial input/turn through `IAgentLauncher.LaunchConnectionRetryAsync` with the persisted `slack-retry:{projectId}:{actionKey}` key and pre-minted IDs, or creates a new follow-up input/turn in the existing Session through the follow-up dispatcher with that same key, preserves the original Connection, actor, conversation, thread, source message, and reply target, and leaves the failed turn immutable.

The SlackRetryOperations migration and store enforce one operation per signed action identity, persist the stable retry dispatch key and pre-minted attempt identities in dispatch-pending before runtime dispatch, record accepted/already-applied/stale/unavailable outcomes and resulting identities, and allow both interaction replay and the fixed-key recovery reminder after a write-before-dispatch failure to resume the same operation and reuse the same dispatch key.

Repeated, concurrently submitted, redelivered, or adapter-failover Retry actions create at most one fresh attempt and converge on the recorded result; a target that is running, completed, cancelled, superseded, unavailable, or otherwise non-retryable starts no attempt and returns the specified terminal state.

Accepted Retry updates the original Slack status target idempotently with acknowledgement and working state plus a rebuilt signed Stop control when applicable; rejected, stale, unavailable, already-applied, and replayed results replace the obsolete Retry control with readable status.

Server unit, integration, store, migration, and terminal-delivery tests cover the exact retryability category matrix, successful root and threaded retries, signature and context rejection, actor authorization, concurrent/replayed operations, process restart after the pending-operation commit, recovery lease takeover, fresh root and follow-up identity creation, immutable failure history, provider-inbox versus button-operation ordering, and durable presentation updates; the focused Server test suite passes.
tasks.output: Retry-operation persistence and migration, terminal Retry rendering, authorized root/thread retry dispatch, durable Slack outcomes, and passing Server coverage.
tasks.notes: Use authoritative persisted session/input provenance for the retry source; never use action-submitted text. Keep the failed attempt immutable and reuse existing launch/follow-up idempotency and status-projection paths.

tasks.title: Deliver single-winner multi-Bot selection for ambiguous Slack messages
tasks.spec: specs/slack-multi-bot-selection/spec.md#Ambiguous prompt state records candidates and one selection outcome
tasks.description: Evolve the workspace-scoped ambiguous prompt record into a durable selection record containing the original source snapshot, actor, thread and prompt delivery identity, ordered candidate descriptors, signed-action metadata, and one selection outcome. Generate a signed choice prompt with a readable fallback, verify and conditionally commit selections in selection-dispatch-pending before dispatch, resume committed selections through the shared fixed-key action-recovery reminder, route the authoritative root or threaded message to exactly one eligible Connection, and replace the prompt controls with an idempotent outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: An ambiguous message mentioning at least two enabled, identity-bound eligible Bots creates no Agent work and results in one durable prompt keyed by workspace, conversation, and message timestamp, with the bounded normalized source text and accepted attachments, actor, thread, prompt delivery identity, ordered candidate set, candidate fingerprint, nonce, expiry, selection state, and dispatch/result references persisted; legacy rows remain readable as text-only prompts.

The winning prompt delivery contains readable candidate names and explicit single-Bot instructions plus exactly one Server-signed action per persisted eligible candidate, is posted at the original root or thread location, and concurrent ingress or redelivery cannot replace its candidate set or create a second prompt delivery.

Selection handling validates the shared signature and expiry plus prompt-owner Connection, workspace, conversation, prompt message or delivery identity, thread, bound actor, candidate fingerprint, selected-candidate eligibility, and current actor access; tampered, unauthorized, expired, wrong-context, stale, and unavailable selections start no work and return explicit outcomes.

A valid root selection dispatches the persisted original message through the selected Connection's normal launch path, while a valid threaded selection uses the selected Connection's existing thread follow-up path when available or its normal thread launch path otherwise; only the selected Connection creates the resulting session/input/turn and owns subsequent status and reply delivery.

The prompt row conditionally records one winner, a stable selection operation, its dispatch key, and selection-dispatch-pending before dispatch, so repeated actions, Slack redelivery, adapter failover, and concurrent different-candidate clicks converge on one winner and one dispatch; a losing candidate returns already-applied or stale without side effects, and a candidate disabled or unauthorized before commit returns unavailable without silent rerouting. The shared recovery reminder claims and resumes a pending winner after process loss without requiring a still-unexpired button.

Accepted, rejected, stale, expired, unauthorized, unavailable, and replayed selections enqueue one idempotent update for the prompt delivery that removes all choice controls, names the selected Bot only when dispatch was accepted, and never claims that unselected work started; interactive delivery failure still leaves the readable fallback path and never infers a candidate.

Server ingress, action, persistence, migration, concurrency, and delivery tests cover root and threaded ambiguity, ineligible mentions, complete candidate persistence, prompt redelivery and delivery recovery, signature/context/actor rejection, original-source routing, existing thread-session follow-up, single-winner races, candidate invalidation, winner commit followed by process restart before dispatch, recovery lease takeover, outcome replacement, source-inbox versus selection-operation ordering, and text fallback; the focused Server test suite passes.
tasks.output: Migration-backed ambiguous prompt selection state, signed interactive choice and fallback delivery, single-winner root/thread routing, durable outcomes, action recovery integration, and passing Server coverage.
tasks.notes: Candidate IDs and source content must come from the durable prompt row, never from redelivered Slack text or an untrusted action value. Preserve the existing stable prompt identity and first-writer-wins behavior while adding conditional winner arbitration. T-002 owns the shared action-recovery reminder; this task integrates selection rows with its pending-operation scan and resume path.
